newsitem.title: USA: U.S. returns three refugees to Cuba, first of year.
newsitem.headline: U.S. returns three refugees to Cuba, first of year.

text.p: The United States Coast Guard returned three Cuban refugees who were picked up in a sailboat off the Florida Keys to Cuba, a Coast Guard spokesman said on Thursday.
They were the first Cubans to be sent back in 1997 under a policy that has enraged Miami's Cuban exile community.

Four Cubans were found drifting in the boat 8 miles (13 km) south of Marathon Key on Monday, Petty Officer Charles Smith said. A Coast Guard cutter took three back to Cabanas Bay on the communist-ruled island on Wednesday.
A fourth was taken to the U.S. military base at Guantanamo, where his claim that he would face persecution if he went back to Cuba would be considered.

Washington, which for years after Cuba's 1958 revolution granted virtually automatic asylum to Cuban refugees, in May last year began returning those picked up at sea. Last month it extended the policy so that Cubans who reached land illegally would also face detention and possible deportation.
